key_insight: The paper shows that separating global temporal modeling from per-time-point spatial refinement can substantially improve EEG source imaging when temporal context is used as a conditioning prior.
engineering_relevance: This decoupled design offers a more accurate and potentially more efficient alternative to fully 4D spatiotemporal networks for inverse EEG reconstruction and transfer to new head geometries.
method: Use a Transformer-based Temporal Condition Encoder to process the full EEG sequence with factorized spatiotemporal attention.
Map the learned temporal representation through a fixed inverse into source-space conditioning for a per-timestep refiner.
Refine sources with either a Source-Space Transformer or a volumetric convolutional model.
evidence_signal: On realistic synthetic EEG, the method outperformed classical and spatiotemporal baselines, especially under high noise and multiple simultaneous sources, and it also transferred to real EEG for age-group decoding from source power differences.
watch_item: Performance depends on synthetic training and operator assumptions, so robustness may vary when leadfield mismatch or real-data distribution shift is stronger than in evaluation.
paper_title: Decoupling Time and Space: A Temporally Conditioned Refinement for EEG Source Imaging
